basis: Developmental disability defines syndrome; hydronephrosis, PDA and strabismus each occur in 30-79%. Milder skull/digital anomalies omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus impairs ocular alignment and occurs in 30-79%; prioritize functional eye disease over mild skeletal dysmorphism.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skull/digital anomalies occur in 30-99%, but are less functionally damaging than retained organs and omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Cobalamin metabolic defect defined by megaloblastic anemia and neurodevelopmental disease; retinopathy 80-99%. Cardiovascular abnormalities 30-79% omitted under cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay, intellectual disability and seizures are explicit defining features, with HPO frequencies of 80-99%.

basis: Hemolytic red-cell disease; intrinsic ischemic bone infarction/necrosis is common (HPO 30-79%). CKD, retinopathy and gallstones are separately diagnosed complications.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: vaso-occlusion results from abnormal erythrocytes; the concept defines a hemoglobinopathy rather than a primary vascular disease.
decisions.renal: none: CKD is annotated at 30-79% but is a separately diagnosed complication; common independent renal damage is not otherwise established here.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: intrinsic vaso-occlusive bone infarction causes structural injury; avascular necrosis is annotated at 30-79%, beyond pain alone.

basis: Severe skeletal dysplasia defines disease. Fatal respiratory distress reflects thoracic restriction; intrinsic pulmonary hypoplasia or injury is not established.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory distress is common (30-79%; most deaths), but a narrow bony thorax does not itself establish direct lung damage.

basis: Acquired clonal blood-cell disease causing complement-sensitive hemolysis; thrombosis is a separately diagnosed complication, not direct defining vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: thrombosis may affect approximately 30-40% over untreated courses, but is a separately diagnosed complication excluded by the rules.

basis: Ataxia, developmental delay and skeletal deformities define syndrome; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Skin hyperextensibility alone does not establish tissue injury.

decisions.dermatologic: none: skin hyperextensibility occurs in 80-99%, but no skin fragility, wounds, scarring or functional loss establishes direct damage.

basis: Mitochondrial spastic ataxia; optic atrophy and ragged-red myofibers each occur in 30-79%, supporting eye and muscle injury. Urinary symptoms are neurogenic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: ragged-red muscle fibers (30-79%) establish intrinsic mitochondrial myofiber pathology alongside common weakness, beyond spasticity alone.

basis: Toxic brain lesions define parkinsonism. Contractures reflect neurologic rigidity; unspecified skin changes do not establish direct skin injury.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: elbow contractures occur in 30-79%, but reflect secondary shortening from neurologic rigidity, without direct joint or muscle disease.

basis: GI polyps and vascular malformations define syndrome; pulmonary AVMs cause shunting in 7/10. Hepatic AVMs (4/7) need not impair liver; anemia reflects blood loss.

decisions.haematologic: none: anemia occurs in 12/14 (~86%), but is secondary to bleeding and separately diagnosed; no intrinsic blood-cell or marrow disorder is established.

basis: MYT1L-related intellectual and developmental disability. Obesity (7/12) is separately diagnosed; singleton strabismus does not establish common ocular involvement.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity occurs in 7/12 (~58%), but is a separately diagnosed associated condition; hyperphagia alone establishes no endocrine organ injury.
